h1: The 8 Best Countertop Ovens for Cooking Pizza at Home, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Pizza Toaster Ovens 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 countertop ovens for homemade and frozen pizza compared on air fry, convection, wattage, capacity and smart features.
summary: The Breville Smart Oven Pro is the best pizza toaster oven if you want a convection oven that holds heat and browns evenly, with the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro a step up for air fry. The Gourmia Indoor Pizza Oven is the best value for a dedicated pizza setup, and the Cuisinart 1800W is a strong, fast mid-priced pick.
intro: Most buyers pick a toaster oven for pizza by looking at slice counts, and the slice count is the least useful number on the page. A pizza cooks well when the oven can reach and hold a hot, even temperature, and when the pie physically fits without the top element scorching the cheese.

So this ranking weighs heat delivery and cooking modes ahead of cavity labels. We reviewed eight countertop ovens from their spec sheets and listings, comparing convection, air fry, wattage, capacity and smart controls. Measurements the listings do not publish, such as maximum pizza diameter, are flagged as items to verify before you order.

products.name: Breville BOV845BSS Smart Oven Pro
products.verdict: A convection Smart Oven that treats pizza as a core job, not an afterthought.
products.description:
The Smart Oven Pro is Breville's convection toaster oven, listed in the $200 to $500 bracket. Convection means a fan circulates hot air through the cavity, which evens out the temperature and removes the cold corners that plague basic toaster ovens.

It takes first place because pizza is a heat-management problem, and Breville's Smart Oven line has built its reputation on managing heat tightly. A convection fan helps the crust set and brown across the whole pie rather than leaving one half pale. Next to the Breville air fryer model below, it gives up the crisping air fry mode, but for pizza that is a minor loss since convection bake is what you use anyway.

Buy it if pizza night is a weekly ritual and you want predictable results. Skip it if your budget stops at $200 or you want air frying as well.
pros: Smart Oven line known for heat control
products.idealFor: Weekly pizza makers who want consistent crust browning.
products.skipIf: You want air frying or a sub-$200 price.

products.name: Breville BOV900BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: The Smart Oven Pro formula with air fry added, for crisping and reheating slices.
products.description:
The Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is Breville's air fry version of its Smart Oven line, listed in the $200 to $500 bracket. It adds an air fry function on top of the usual toaster oven modes.

It ranks second because air fry makes it the more versatile appliance, even though pizza itself does not need it. Air frying is excellent for reheating leftover slices so the crust crisps again rather than going rubbery, and the same oven handles wings, fries and roasted vegetables. For first bakes of a fresh pie, the standard convection settings do most of the work. The tradeoff is cost: you pay for versatility you may use only occasionally.

Pick it if you want one oven to replace a toaster, an air fryer and a pizza oven. Skip it if pizza is the only job.
cons: Air fry is optional for pizza
products.idealFor: Households wanting a single oven for everything.
products.skipIf: You only need pizza and can skip air fry.

products.name: Gourmia Electric Indoor Pizza Oven - Countertop Air Fryer Toaster
products.verdict: An indoor pizza oven that doubles as an air fryer toaster, at a mid-tier price.
products.description:
The Gourmia is sold as an electric indoor pizza oven with air fry in a countertop toaster format, priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. It is the only model in this ranking that markets pizza in its name.

It places third because it pairs a pizza-first design with a price well under the Breville ovens. The listing gives no wattage, temperature ceiling or interior dimensions, so judge it cautiously; a dedicated pizza oven usually runs hotter than a standard toaster oven, which is the point of buying one. The risk is that detail is thin and a premium brand carries more proven calibration.

Choose it if you want a pizza-focused oven without the Breville price. Skip it if you need verified specs, since the listing is short on numbers.
pros: Built around pizza from the name
products.idealFor: Pizza fans who want a dedicated oven on a mid budget.
products.skipIf: You want exact wattage and temperature figures.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: 1800 watts of heating power and air fry from a name that makes ovens for a living.
products.description:
The Cuisinart is an air fryer toaster oven rated at 1800 watts, listed in the $100 to $200 bracket. The wattage figure is the useful number: it indicates how much power the heating elements can pull to recover temperature after you open the door.

It ranks fourth because power helps with pizza, where a loaded pie needs a strong blast of heat to cook the top and bottom before the crust dries. Most home outlets support 1800 watts, which is close to the usable limit for a plug-in appliance. Compared with the Gourmia above, it has a clear wattage figure; compared with the Brevilles, it lacks the same smart heat control.

Buy it if you want a strong, no-frills air fry toaster oven from a trusted kitchen brand. Skip it if you share a circuit with other high-draw appliances.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want strong heating at a fair price.
products.skipIf: Your kitchen circuit is already crowded.

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro Air Fryer Toaster Oven w/Grill Combo
products.verdict: An air fryer, toaster and grill combo that handles pizza as one of many jobs.
products.description:
The Nuwave Bravo XL Pro is an air fryer toaster oven with a grill combination, listed in the $200 to $500 bracket. The XL in the name signals a larger cavity than a basic toaster oven.

It ranks fifth because it is more of a multi-tool than a pizza specialist. The grill function is handy for finishing the top of a pizza or melting cheese, and the air fry mode crisps leftovers. At the same price band as the Breville ovens, it offers less proven pizza performance, though it adds a grill most competitors lack.

Go for it if you want to grill, air fry and bake pizza from one appliance. Skip it if pizza is your priority and you can afford the Smart Oven.
pros: Grill function melts and chars cheese
Many cooking modes in one box
products.idealFor: Multi-tasking cooks who want a grill function.
products.skipIf: You want pizza performance above all.

products.name: KitchenAid Digital Countertop Oven
products.verdict: A digital-control countertop oven with air fry from a well-known baking brand.
products.description:
The KitchenAid Digital Countertop Oven combines digital controls with an air fry function. The listing gives few other specs, and no price tier is published.

It ranks sixth because a name and a control panel alone do not tell you how it handles a pizza. Digital temperature setting is a real advantage over dial ovens, since you can dial in an exact number and keep returning to it for repeat bakes. The unknown is capacity and wattage, which you should confirm on the product page before relying on it for a full-size pie.

Buy it if you value precise digital controls and want a trusted kitchen brand. Skip it if you want hard numbers on heat output and pizza size before you buy.
cons: Few specs published in the listing
products.idealFor: Bakers who like exact digital temperature control.
products.skipIf: You need confirmed size and wattage first.

products.name: Typhur Sync Oven with Smart Wireless Meat Thermometer Probe
products.verdict: An air fry oven with a wireless meat probe, more roast-focused than pizza-focused.
products.description:
The Typhur Sync Oven pairs air frying with a smart wireless meat thermometer probe, listed in the $100 to $200 bracket. The probe is the headline, since it tracks the internal temperature of roasts and chicken.

It places seventh because the probe does nothing for pizza. The air fry mode still crisps a reheated slice, but the oven's best features serve roasting. If you cook a lot of meat and want the pizza capability as a secondary job, it is competitive; if pizza comes first, the Gourmia and Cuisinart are better aimed.

Choose it if you roast regularly and want pizza as a bonus. Skip it if pizza night is the main reason to buy.
pros: Good for roasts and pizza together
products.idealFor: Cooks who roast meat more than they bake pizza.
products.skipIf: Pizza night is the main job.

products.name: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Multi-Function Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A roomy 26 quart air fry oven with French doors, handy for loading pizza.
products.description:
The Emeril Lagasse oven has a 26 quart cavity, French doors and multi-function air frying, listed in the $100 to $200 bracket. The French doors open outward from the centre, which makes sliding a pizza on a peel or tray easier than with a drop-down door.

It ranks last because the listing does not describe heat output or pizza-specific settings. It does offer a good amount of cavity space for the price and a design that is friendlier to load. Check the interior width against the size of your pizza before buying.

Buy it if you value easy access and a large cavity at a moderate price. Skip it if you want proven convection performance.
products.idealFor: Families who want easy access and room to cook.
products.skipIf: You want a proven convection pizza oven.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is the heating elements' maximum draw, and it determines how quickly the oven recovers after the door opens. Pizza benefits from strong, fast heat so the top and bottom finish together. Look for a wattage figure on the listing, with 1800W near the ceiling for a plug-in oven.

Convection circulates air gently for even browning, which suits a first bake of a fresh or frozen pie. Air fry runs the fan harder to crisp food, which is ideal for reheating a slice. Check which modes the listing names and do not assume both.

A pizza needs interior width a little larger than its diameter, plus clearance so the cheese does not touch the top element. Slice counts and quarts are poor proxies. Check the manual or product page for the largest pizza size it supports.

A drop-down door can make sliding a pizza on or off awkward, while French doors open from the centre. Door design affects how easily you can load a peel or tray. Consider how often you will open the oven mid-bake.

Digital controls let you repeat the same temperature every time, and smart probes help with meat rather than pizza. Prioritise a clear temperature readout over extra features. Look for the maximum temperature and whether the oven preheats quickly.

faq.q: Can a toaster oven cook a full-size pizza?
faq.a: It depends on interior width, which is rarely on the main listing. Check the manual or product page for the largest pizza size, because a pie that touches the heating element will scorch.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a pizza toaster oven?
faq.a: Choosing by slice count or quarts instead of heat and width. A large cavity with weak heating cooks a pizza unevenly, while a smaller strong oven can do better.

faq.q: Is a Breville worth it over a cheaper oven?
faq.a: For weekly pizza, yes: the Smart Oven line is built around heat management and convection. If you bake pizza rarely, the Cuisinart or Gourmia is enough.

faq.q: How should I preheat for pizza?
faq.a: Preheat fully to the target temperature before sliding the pizza in, and use the rack position the manual recommends. A short extra preheat helps the oven recover when you open the door.

faq.q: How do I clean a toaster oven used for pizza?
faq.a: Let the oven cool, empty the crumb tray, and wipe the interior with a damp cloth and mild soap. Scrape baked-on cheese before it hardens, and avoid abrasive pads on coated surfaces.

faq.q: Does air fry work for pizza?
faq.a: It works best for reheating leftover slices, where the fan crisps the crust again. For a fresh pie, convection or standard bake is usually gentler and more even.

finalTake: The Breville Smart Oven Pro is the best pizza toaster oven because convection and careful heat control matter more to a crust than any extra feature. Step up to the Air Fryer Pro if you also want crisping, or save with the Gourmia or Cuisinart for a solid mid-price bake. Skip ovens that publish no wattage or pizza size until you have confirmed the numbers.
